parsed.main_gap: The proof that a nonunit always remains uses the false principle that a positive, nonincreasing integer sequence cannot reach zero.

errors.description: A nonincreasing nonnegative integer starting positive can reach zero. The needed conclusion is nevertheless easily repaired: every legal move leaves at least one selected replacement greater than 1—gcd(m,n) if it exceeds 1, otherwise mn.
errors.quote: A nonnegative integer that never increases and starts at a positive value can never reach \(0\); hence \(K\ge1\) at every stage

parsed.notes: Apart from this localized gap, the lexicographic descent proves termination, and the primewise gcd invariant correctly determines the unique terminal value.
